questions.question: Explain what acid mine drainage is and why it is harmful.
questions.expected_answer: Rocks in gold and coal mines contain pyrite, which reacts with air and water to form acid. When old mines close, the pumps stop and the tunnels fill with water, which becomes acidic and dissolves metals like iron and manganese. This orange, polluted water flows out into streams and rivers, where it can kill fish and plants, make water unsafe to drink, harm crops and damage pipes.

questions.question: Describe how mining pollutes the air.
questions.expected_answer: Blasting, crushing, trucks on dirt roads and wind over mine dumps send dust into the air, which can cause coughing, asthma and lung problems. Smelters and coal-fired power stations release smoke and gases such as sulphur dioxide, which can cause acid rain, and carbon dioxide, which adds to climate change. On the Mpumalanga Highveld, pollution gets trapped on still winter mornings.

questions.question: How can water and air pollution from mining be reduced?
questions.expected_answer: Mines can line dams, treat polluted water and keep clean water separate, and the government treats acid mine water. Dust can be reduced by spraying water, covering conveyors and planting grass on dumps. Filters in chimneys reduce smoke and gases, and solar and wind power reduce coal burning. Inspectors enforce the law, and communities can test and report pollution.
